notice: These English descriptions record visible features inspected in original embedded images and per-lesson contact sheets. They are not original textbook wording, teacher-approved interpretations or live travel facts. Preview rendering omits some selectable Chinese and Thai glyphs; use extracted OOXML text for those words. No missing glyph is transcribed from the defective previews. A readable source PDF would permit more reliable layout and answer-position verification.

observations.description: Airport, aircraft and travellers with luggage provide the arrival context. Red star marks highlight selected words in vocabulary tables; no mastery level is inferred from the stars.
House, hotel and airport pictures are used with connecting arrows to illustrate destinations and relative distance. This is a schematic language illustration, not a navigable map or measured route.
The embedded yellow sign contains the visible text 请稍等 and PLEASE WAIT, supporting the waiting expressions in the selectable text.
Passport, boarding-pass and immigration-counter illustrations support the document/enquiry dialogue. They do not establish present visa procedures or required documents.
Photographs of buildings, a Buddhist statue and a floating-market scene accompany the named destinations. Do not identify an unlabeled photograph as a particular attraction solely from appearance.
A hotel, temple-style building and airport are connected by differently curved blue arrows to illustrate 离 and distance. No scale, street names or geographic route is provided.
Reception, service-staff and occupation illustrations support hotel welcome vocabulary and the 员 word family.
A hand using a room card at a door is contrasted with a bank-card image and a SIM-card image, illustrating different kinds of 卡.
The total 3,000 is emphasized in the payment dialogue. A room doorway, luggage and a staff member support the request for permission to enter.
Taxi, tuk-tuk and phone/app-booking illustrations accompany transport expressions. The source includes Grab as a named app in the dialogue; there is no implemented app integration.
Straight, left and right arrows support direction language. The branching montage of destination/travel photographs is illustrative; it is not a real street map.
A ticket icon, money symbols, the English word FREE and the number 500 visualize fee vocabulary and the source admission-price example.
Images of renminbi and Thai banknotes distinguish currencies. The practice panels visibly show 2,000 RMB and 5,000 Baht; they do not supply a currency conversion rate.
A bank, hospital, restaurant, palace, school, airport, market and hotel are shown as destination/purpose prompts for 去+地方+做什么.

Clock, motorcycle and warning-symbol illustrations accompany the duration and transport-choice discussion. Source estimates 10, 5 and 7 are displayed; the warning does not establish a universal safety ranking.

Two columns of transport pictures illustrate aircraft, ship, metro/train, bus, taxi, motorcycle, car, bicycle and tuk-tuk vocabulary. Some pictures are generic transport illustrations rather than Thai location evidence.
Coffee/tea, rice/noodles, singing/dancing, transport, attraction and currency pairs provide visible alternatives for 还是 practice.

Night-market/crowd photos, singing, fruit/durian, temple and travel illustrations support the market and temple dialogues. The three EMF placements on S4/S6/S8 remain in the original PPT and appear in the full-slide previews.
An embedded fruit-section sign visibly reads 水果区 and SHUIGUOQU. This text belongs to an image and is distinct from the selectable title 学习泰国常见的10种水果.

Fruit photographs/illustrations accompany the selectable Chinese labels. Slide 10 labels 橙子、香蕉、西瓜、菠萝、菠萝蜜. Slide 11 labels 山竹、红毛丹、椰子、莲雾、芒果. Use the extracted label blocks and original placement for matching.

An unlabeled collage shows ten fruit illustrations: pineapple, mangosteen, coconut, jackfruit, banana, durian, orange, rambutan, mango and wax-apple-like fruit. These are editorial visual identifications, not a transcription of missing textbook labels. The image-only slide remains flagged for teacher review.
A classroom/bookshelf and pictures of an airport crowd, loaded car, hotel reception, market boats and roadside tuk-tuks illustrate place+有+people/things.

Hikers, mountain scenes, tired/happy figures, a coat and hot/cold icons support hiking and A-not-A questions. The mountain photographs have not been independently verified as Doi Suthep, and the temperature icons are not a weather forecast.
Noodle-dish photographs, a menu illustration, chef/stir-frying and restaurant-service scenes support ordering and checking a dish. Photographs alone cannot verify ingredients or dietary suitability.
Bills, cash/payment icons and the prominently displayed number 160 support the source payment exchange. This amount is a scenario total.
A calendar image with circled dates supports date questions. Do not infer a present calendar year or current flight date from this reused illustration.
Analogue clocks, boarding-stairs/crew illustrations and travellers with luggage support clock time, boarding and departure. The source text distinguishes departure at one from boarding at three.
Beach photographs and a PHUKET sign accompany description language. An unlabeled beach photograph is not proof of an exact named location.
A vertical palette shows blue, yellow, red, green, purple, black and white swatches, supporting the selectable colour list.
Parasailing, watercraft, shopping and location-pin pictures support the activities and 旁边 vocabulary. Activity pictures are descriptive course material, not a safety endorsement.

Electronic-product and clothing diagrams support non-tabular vocabulary. Directional pointers surround a dressed figure to indicate clothing items; inspect original labels rather than guessing their missing preview glyphs.

A vertical numbered floor diagram shows 1 beside a supermarket image, 2 beside clothing and 3 beside electronics. It visualizes the dialogue's exercise layout, not a verified current shopping-centre directory.

A fruit montage contains Chinese/pinyin labels embedded in the bitmap, in addition to selectable 芒果/新鲜. The bitmap is retained at its original resolution for transcription verification; unclear spellings must be checked directly rather than normalized.
Colourful shopfront/street photographs and group-of-people illustrations establish an evening street/market context. They do not supply a current operating schedule.

Leaf colours, green/red apples, running/tired figures, sun/rain, crying/smiling and before/after body/hair pictures visualize change. For a Grade 11 adaptation, discuss changes sensitively rather than using appearance to judge people.
Sun-on-the-horizon, beach and island imagery supports sunrise/trip suggestions. The images cannot establish viewing direction, exact location or whether a proposed sunrise visit is suitable.
Uncaptioned activity prompts include a street visit, beach, temple, travel, shopping, dining, singing, watercraft, parasailing and swimming, supporting suggestions with 怎么样.
Café/restaurant, shop, hotel, bookshop and beach images illustrate establishment words. A 2 m spacing pictogram appears beside distance language; it is an illustration, not a measured route.

Food and drink montages support the source vocabulary: noodle dishes, fried chicken, grilled meat, salad, sticky rice, soups, fish, crab and fruit drinks. Non-tabular dish/drink labels remain in the selectable text; pictures cannot confirm recipes or allergens.

A watermelon/apple size comparison, pencils of different lengths and figures of different height/body size provide A比B / A没有B prompts. A 0.3 m height difference is printed in the source; no other quantity should be inferred from drawing scale.

Pictures distinguish sky lanterns in the air from floating water lanterns; cloud/boat examples support 飘. The illustrations depict source festival imagery and do not establish contemporary permissions or environmental acceptability.

A banana plant/leaf, flowers, candle and completed water lantern visualize the source materials. On slide 12 these graphics provide meaningful answer context where the selectable dialogue omits the material-list line.
Food/chilli and frightened-person/dog illustrations support strong-degree expressions, including non-adjectival feeling vocabulary in the source examples.
Flags illustrate Thailand, China, the United States, Japan and South Korea. A flag is a vocabulary cue, not evidence that every individual follows one greeting practice.

Handshake, bowing, palms-together greeting and a wrapped gift visualize the different contexts of 见面礼. Hand position details require the source explanation and teacher confirmation, not inference from simplified cartoons.

Paired flowers, pencils, dresses, greeting scenes and different-height figures support similarity/difference prompts. The two pencils differ in length and the dresses differ in size/colour; the prompt does not require a guessed answer key.
Water-fight, water-gun, wet-clothing and festival photographs/illustrations provide Songkran context. The source also includes other activity examples such as basketball and shopping.

Growth stages, increased workload/tiredness, different body size, hair loss and eating illustrations cue degree changing over time. Some are appearance-focused and should be discussed carefully; they do not measure an actual person.

Flowers, thanks/greeting images, ceremony/festival photos and a teacher touching a child's head accompany gratitude and blessing language. These images are source representations rather than prescribed actions for all participants.
Wrapped gifts, an open box, chocolate and a flower basket distinguish gift vocabulary and the speakers' choices. The box/chocolate/basket relationship is retained in the original slide layout.

Giving flowers, putting money in a bank, placing books in a bag, disposing of a banana skin, cutting tomatoes, delivering a box, a cat with a flower and putting 福 on a door illustrate different 把 complements. The 你好 / Hello icon supports the transformation example 翻译成.

Temple/building photographs, Buddha/temple illustrations, clothing/shoes and a crossed-out shoe pictogram support temple-visit dialogue. Photograph identities and site rules have not been independently verified.
An embedded before/after timeline visibly includes 以前 and 以后, supporting the selectable 以前—现在—以后 examples.

Prohibition pictograms depict no smoking, no littering, no photography, no swimming, no telephone calls and quietness. They support 不要 practice in source scenarios; they are not universal rules for every temple, school, hospital or beach.
